parole.testo: Perhaps from Akkadian 𒌓𒅗𒁇 (UD.KA.BAR /⁠agannu⁠/).
The "letter" sense may be borrowed from Akkadian 𒂊𒄈𒌅 (egertu). The "roof" sense may be from Aramaic, from Akkadian 𒂍𒋞 (igārum, “wall”).

Most likely a loan word from Akkadian 𒄀𒁍 (ebbūbum, “flute”), which probably derived from the root n-b-b (to be hollow). Compare Arabic أُنْبُوب (ʔunbūb, “pipe, tube”). The Modern Hebrew sense is a phono-semantic matching of English oboe.
Borrowed into West Semitic from Akkadian 𒀀𒂵𒈬𒌝 (agammum), from Sumerian 𒀀𒂵𒄠 (agam). Compare Classical Syriac ܐܓܡܐ (ʾaḡmā, “marsh, swamp”) and Arabic أَجَمَة (ʔajama, “jungle, brushwood”).

Uncertain; doublet of אֵלוֹן (elón), which possibly is the native Canaanite counterpart, compare Aramaic אִילָנָא (ʾīlānā, “tree”) and Classical Syriac ܐܺܝܠܳܢܳܐ (ʾīlānā, “tree”). The present form with a short /a/ and a geminated /l/ on the other hand may be a borrowing from Akkadian 𒀠𒆷𒀭 (ʾallānu, al
Borrowed from Akkadian 𒋠𒍝𒆳𒋛𒀀 (argamannu).

parole.significato: Tyrian purple, or a garment dyed with it (a purple-dye associated with royalty, as it was very expensive to produce)
parole.testo: Uncertain, possibly borrowed from Akkadian 𒋠𒍝𒆳𒋛𒀀 (argamannu).
Coined by Eliezer Ben-Yehuda from Akkadian 𒌑𒊒𒁺𒌑 (urudû, “copper”), itself a borrowing from Sumerian 𒍏 (urudu).

parole.significato: fir, a tree of the genus Abies
parole.testo: Borrowed from Akkadian 𒄑𒅇𒆪 (^(GIŠ)Ù.SUḪ₅ /⁠ašūḫu⁠/), from Hurrian 𒀸𒌋𒄭 (AŠ.U.ḪI /⁠ašoḫe⁠/, “fir; mealtime (due to cooking fumes)”). Compare Aramaic אַשׁוּחָא, Assyrian Neo-Aramaic ܫܘܚܐ (šwḥā), and Arabic شُوح (šūḥ).

Derived from Akkadian 𒂡 (isinnu, išinnu, “festival, fixed time”), from Sumerian 𒂡 (ezem, ezen /⁠ezem⁠/, “festival”), which is possibly a borrowing from Semitic languages itself (comp. Arabic مَوْسِم (mawsim, “season, festival”)).

parole.significato: Assyrian (a citizen of an ancient nation and empire, including the northern half of Mesopotamia, with capital city of N…
parole.testo: From אַשּׁוּר m (ashúr, ʾaššûr, “Assyria; Assyrian nation; Ashur, grandson of Noah”), ultimately from Akkadian 𒀸𒋩𒆠 (Aššūr, “Assur”), name of Assyria's original capital city, and its eponymous god.

From Akkadian āšipu (“sorcerer, magician, exorcist, incantation priest”). Compare Aramaic אשפא and Classical Syriac ܐܫܘܦܐ. According to Midrash Tanhuma, derived from שָׁאַף (“to trample, to crush, to press”), a secondary form of שָׁף.
Borrowed from Akkadian 𒌑𒁍𒌓𒉡 (/⁠buṭnu⁠/, “terebinth”), related to Arabic بُطْم (buṭm).

parole.significato: a get, a document effecting the divorce of a wife from her husband
parole.testo: Probably from Akkadian 𒁍𒁕 (gídda /⁠giṭṭu⁠/, “document or deed written on parchment”), from Sumerian 𒁍𒁕 (gid₂-da, “length”), from Sumerian 𒁍 (gid₂, “to drag, to draw up a document”). Compare Classical Syriac ܓܛܐ (geṭṭā, “will, testament, document”), in other Aramaic dialects, a narrowed sense of "wri
Borrowed from Akkadian 𒄀𒅖𒊒 (gišru, “bridge”).
Borrowed from Akkadian 𒁾 (ṭuppum, “tablet”), itself borrowed from Sumerian 𒁾 (dub, “tablet”), compare Aramaic דַּפָּא (dappā, “page, tablet”).

Borrowed from Akkadian 𒀭𒁺𒊏𒊒 (andurāru, “remission of debts, manumission of slaves, cancelling of illegal impositions on free persons”) or 𒁕𒊏𒊒 (darāru, “freedom; to become free of a task, to move about freely, to run off”).

parole.significato: camelthorn (Alhagi, a genus of shrubs native to northern Africa and Asia Minor)
parole.testo: Related to Jewish Babylonian Aramaic הֵיגְתָא (heg'ta) and Classical Syriac ܚܵܓܬ݂ܵܐ (ḥāggəṯāʾ), all derived from Akkadian 𒂊𒄖𒌋 (egû). First attested in the Talmud.
From Akkadian 𒂍𒃲 (ēkallum), from Sumerian 𒂍𒃲 (e₂-gal /⁠ēgal⁠/). Cognate with Arabic هَيْكَل (haykal) and Aramaic הֵיכְלָא (hēḵəlā).
Action noun of the verb הִקִּיף (“to surround, to circle, to sell on credit”). In sense 5, possibly borrowed from Akkadian [script needed] (qiāpu, “to believe, to make a loan, to extend credit”).
Learned borrowing from Akkadian 𒅆𒂍𒉪 (ziqqurratum).

parole.significato: cantor; leader of a congregation or other group in prayer
parole.testo: Probably borrowed from Akkadian 𒄩𒍝𒀭𒉡 (ḫazannu).

parole.significato: a type of cake used in sacrifices to a pagan goddess (most likely Astarte/Ishtar)
parole.testo: Uncertain, most likely from Akkadian [Term?] (/⁠kamānum⁠/, “a loaf/bread/cake sometimes used in sacrifices”). Compare χαυών (khauṓn). Alternatively, according to Gesenius, from the root כ־ו־ן (“firmness, establishment, preparing”).

Derived from Akkadian 𒆠𒉈 (/⁠kuru⁠/, “crucible, kiln, brazier; log, thick reed; short reed mat, collection of reeds”), likely coined from Sumerian 𒄥 (gur, “a bundle”), hence a place of burning bundles of firewood or tinder. Cognate with Aramaic כּוּרָא (kūrā), Classical Syriac ܟܘܪܐ (kūrā), Arabic كُو

parole.significato: A biblical measure of weight equal to 10 ephah.
parole.testo: From Akkadian 𒄥 (/⁠kurru⁠/), from Sumerian 𒄥 (GUR, “a bundle of barley; standard unit of capacity”). Cognate with Aramaic כּוֹרָא (kōrā, “a dry measure”), Classical Syriac ܟܘܪܐ (kōrā, “a dry measure”), Arabic كُرّ (kurr, “a dry measure; payment of six donkeys”).
From Akkadian 𒄑𒄖𒍝 (kussûm).

From Akkadian 𒂵𒆜𒊬 (GA.KASKAL^(SAR), GA.RAŠ^(SAR) /⁠karašu⁠/), from Sumerian 𒂵𒆜𒊬 (GA.KASKAL^(SAR), GA.RAŠ^(SAR) /⁠garaš⁠/). Also Aramaic כרתא / ܟܪܬܐ (karrāṯā), whence Arabic كَرَّاث (karrāṯ), also Maltese kurrat whence Middle Armenian, Armenian քուռաթ (kʻuṙatʻ).

From Akkadian 𒆳𒆗𒁺 (/⁠Kaldu⁠/), variant of 𒅗𒃻𒁺 (/⁠Kašdu⁠/), either by dissimilation or as a rendering of the Proto-Semitic voiceless lateral fricative *ś. Cognate of Aramaic כַּשְׂדָּי (kaśdāy, “Chaldean”).

A loanword from Akkadian 𒊩𒆤𒇲 (lilû, lilītu, “demon”), from Sumerian [Term?] (/⁠lil⁠/, “demon”). Associated by folk etymology with לַיְלָה (láylā, “night”), hence transferred to a nocturnal demon and nocturnal bird.
Likely from Akkadian 𒌓𒁕 (manzaltum). Compare Aramaic מַזָּלָא (mazzālā, “constellation; luck, destiny”) (Classical Mandaic ࡌࡀࡍࡆࡀࡋࡀ (manzala, “constellation; zodiac sign”)).
Probably borrowed from Akkadian [script needed] (maḫīru, “purchase price”), from Akkadian [script needed] (maḥām, “to receive, get, buy”).
From Akkadian 𒈣𒁻 (malāḫum, “shipman, sailor”), from Sumerian 𒈣𒁻 (ma₂-laḫ₄ /⁠malaḫ⁠/, “shipman, sailor”). Cognate with Arabic مَلَّاح (mallāḥ).
Of Akkadian origin. From Akkadian 𒀵𒂍𒃲 (maṣṣaru, “a guard”).

parole.significato: beam (ploughbeam), the beam of a loom
parole.testo: See also Arabic نِير (nīr), Aramaic נִירָא / ܢܺܝܪܳܐ (nīrā); from Akkadian 𒉌𒄿𒊒 (nīru, “yoke, crossbeam”).

Used in the Bible (Ecclesiastes 9:15). Compare Aramaic (see for example the Targum of the word עני in Deut. 24:12). From Akkadian 𒈦𒆕𒂗 (muškēnum, “beggar, needy, indigent; class of people dependent or reliant on others, unable to provide supplies on their own; commoner”).
Borrowed from Akkadian 𒇽𒈬 (nuḫatimmu, “cook, chef”), itself from Sumerian 𒇽𒈬 (muḫaldim). Compare Aramaic נַחְתּוֹמָא.
From Akkadian 𒉌𒆳𒊏 (napṭu, “naphtha”), similar to Classical Syriac ܢܦܛܐ.

parole.significato: seah, an ancient Hebrew unit equivalent to ⅓ of an ephah.
parole.testo: From Akkadian 𒊺 (še'um, “grain, measure of grain”), from Sumerian 𒊺 (še, “barley, grain”). Compare Aramaic סָאתָא (sāʾṯā). Unrelated to Arabic صَاع (ṣāʕ, “ṣāʿ”), Ge'ez ጽዋዕ (ṣəwaʿ, “cup, chalice”), Aramaic צעא (“bowl”), and Ugaritic 𐎕𐎓 (ṣʿ, “plate, platter”).
Borrowed from Akkadian 𒄑𒄿𒇻 (simmiltum, “stair; stairs; ladder”) with metathesis. Cognate with Aramaic סוּלַם (sulam), Arabic سُلَّم (sullam), borrowed from the same etymon.
Likely borrowed from Akkadian 𒅆𒅁𒀸 (šiprum, “message, report”). Compare Aramaic סִפְרָא (sip̄rā, “book”) and Arabic سِفْر (sifr, “book”).
Borrowed from Akkadian ša rēši (literally “who is at the head”), cognate to זֶה + רֹאשׁ. The root ס־ר־ס (s-r-s) is denominative.

Cognate with Aramaic עַלֵּם (ʿallem) "to conceal, make disappear" and Ugaritic 𐎓𐎍𐎎 (ʿlm) "to be hidden, unknown; to go unnoticed". Potentially related to Akkadian 𒂖𒆷𒈬𒌋𒀀 (/⁠ellamu, illamu⁠/, “front, before; both temporally and in location; coming before your time or being currently physically before

Cognate with Ugaritic 𐎓𐎍𐎎 (ʿlm) "eternity", Phoenician 𐤏𐤋𐤌 (ʿlm) "eternity", Aramaic עָלַם (ʿālam) "eternity; world, universe; nation, people", Arabic عَالَم (ʕālam) "world", and Ge'ez ዓለም (ʿaläm) "world" (the latter two likely borrowed from Aramaic). Potentially also related to Akkadian 𒂖𒆷𒈬𒌋𒀀 (/⁠el

Related to Hebrew עֵדֶן (éden, ʿēden, “Eden”), derived from Akkadian 𒂊𒁲𒉡 (edinu, “plain, lowland; wilds, steppes; land naturally irrigated, untouched fertile land”), a loan from Sumerian 𒂔 (eden, “plain, open country”).
Borrowed from Akkadian 𒎎𒁓 (pūrum, literally “stone bowl, lot”) from Sumerian 𒁓 (bur).
From Akkadian pīḫātu (province), probably an ellipsis of bêl pīḫāti (literally “lord of the province”). The second meaning is a phono-semantic matching of Turkish paşa.
From Akkadian 𒆠𒅖𒌝 (kišum).
Borrowed from Akkadian šubû (“agate”), from Sumerian šuba (“multicolored”).

parole.significato: Shabbat, Sabbath; weekly day of rest
parole.testo: Possibly borrowed from Akkadian 𒊭𒉺𒀜𒌈 (šapattum, “the middle day of the lunar month”).

From Talmudic Hebrew, from Akkadian 𒅆𒂍𒌈 (/⁠šibittu⁠/); cognate to Persian شوید (ševid), Jewish Babylonian Aramaic שִׁיבְתָא (šiḇəṯā), Classical Syriac ܫܒܬܐ. (Arabic شِبِثّ (šibiṯṯ) comes via Aramaic.)
Believed to have originally meant "scribe", and translated thus in the Septuagint, it is likely ultimately derived from Akkadian 𒊬 (šaṭārum, “to write, to inscribe, to jot down”).
From Akkadian 𒌑𒄩 (šimru, “fennel”). See Arabic شَمَر (šamar, “fennel”) for other cognates. Largely displaced the native Hebrew synonym גּוּפְנָן (gup̄nān, “fennel”).

parole.significato: market in the broad sense of the word
parole.testo: Probably from Akkadian 𒋻 (sūqum, “street”). Compare Arabic سُوق (sūq).

The almond-name is akin to Phoenician 𐤔𐤒𐤃 (šqd, “almond; almond-tree”), Ugaritic 𐎘𐎖𐎄 (ṯqd, “almond; almond-tree”), Jewish Literary Aramaic, Jewish Babylonian Aramaic שִׁגּדּא (šigdā), Classical Syriac ܫܓܕܐ (šegdā, “almond”, collective), only Hebraized שִׁקְדּא (šiqdā) and ܫܩܕܐ (šeqdā), Aramaic-borro

parole.significato: stool (a seat, especially for one person and without armrests)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Akkadian [script needed] (šupal šapi) with metathesis and dissimilatory exchange of the liquid /l/ with /r/. Compare (rare) שַׁרְשִׁיף (sharshíf).
Already in Canaanite times loaned from Akkadian [script needed] (satālu).
Cognate with Aramaic תִּבְנָא / ܬܒܢܐ (teḇnā, “straw”) whence Arabic تِبْن (tibn) and cognate to or derived from Akkadian 𒅔𒉡𒁕 (/⁠tibnu⁠/, “straw”).
From Akkadian 𒊑𒈪𒁺 (talmīdu). Cognate with Aramaic תלמידא (talmīḏā).

Loanword from Akkadian 𒅎𒋗𒆸 (tinūrum). Compare also Middle Persian tnwl (tanūr, “oven”). This word has been borrowed into Aramaic as תנורא / ܬܰܢܽܘܪܳܐ (tannūrā) and therethrough spawned Arabic تَنُّور (tannūr).

Derived from Akkadian 𒆗𒉌𒉡 (danninu, “netherworld; source of earthquakes; the inaccessible land where the dead remain”), whence also Aramaic תַּנִּינָא / ܬܱܢܺܝܢܳܐ (tannīnā, “sea serpent, monster”) and Ugaritic 𐎚𐎐𐎐 (tnn).

parole.significato: chicken, either male or of unspecified gender
parole.testo: From Akkadian 𒁯𒈗𒄷 (tarlugallum, “rooster”), from Sumerian 𒁯𒈗𒄷 (dar-lugal^(mušen) /⁠darlugal⁠/, “rooster”, literally “bird or fowl of the king”). The first element uncertainly connected to Proto-Semitic *ṭayr- (“bird”) or Proto-Semitic *dVrr, Proto-Afroasiatic *dir(h)w- (“bird, hen, dove, fowl, chick
Either borrowed from Aramaic אִכָּרָא (“farmer”) or Akkadian 𒇽𒀳 (ikkarum); compare also Classical Syriac ܐܟܪܐ (ʾakkārā).

(village): From Aramaic כַּפְרָא / ܟܰܦܪܳܐ (kap̄rā, “village, open town, unfortified town”), from Akkadian 𒅗𒀊𒊒 (kapru, “farm, village; a settlement outside of a city”), considered to be from the non-Akkadian “Mari language”, that is it is formed either in the unknown East Semitic or the unknown Amori

In Biblical Hebrew attested twice ambiguously: In the First Book of Kings 7:50 either “front side” or “socket of the door pin” of a door; in the Book of Isaiah 3:17 skulls of women are made scabby and their פֹּת (pōṯ) bared, where it is natural to assume it to mean “foreheads” rather than “pudenda”;

Borrowed from Aramaic שַׁרְשִׁיפָא (“footstool”), itself either borrowed from Mishnaic Hebrew שְׁרַפְרַף (šərafraf) or from the theoretical Aramaic cognate שרפרפא; Further etymology debated, possibilities include: * From Akkadian 𒆠𒋫 (šupāl(u/i), “low-lying area”) + Akkadian 𒄊 (šēpi, “feet”) with met
